quote: So low activity matters far more when spend is also falling. ... Last lesson's weighted sum gave each column one weight for everyone.
problem: The numbers offered as an 'it depends' the tree found and a weighted sum cannot express are not an interaction on the scale the weighted sum works on. Low activity multiplies the odds of churn by about 4 in both columns (4.0 when spend holds, 4.5 when it shrinks), which a single weight per column reproduces through the S-curve - exactly what 3-2 seg3 taught ('the same push moves an advertiser near 50 percent a long way'). The general claim about trees is right; this evidence does not show it.
evidence: tree.root: 0.053 -> 0.182 (odds 0.056 -> 0.222, x4.0) and 0.211 -> 0.544 (odds 0.267 -> 1.193, x4.5). Consistent with logreg beating the tree (0.845 vs 0.761).
fix: Say the gap is in percentage points ("13 points when spend holds, 33 when it shrinks") and rest the 'it depends' point on what the tree really does differently: each branch picks its own next question and cut-off (size on one branch, click rate on the other).

quote: test AUC above 0.95 ... the two sides churn at 94 percent and 1 percent
problem: A course-domain question states specific results for a leaky tree on this data (its AUC, the split at 30 days, the two branch rates) that are not in facts.json and cannot be derived; facts only hold the leak's effect on the logistic regression.
evidence: leakage.auc_with_leak = 0.97 is for logistic regression; leakage has medians 86 vs 3 and leak_metrics_at_half (precision 0.975) but no tree split or branch rates.
fix: Drop the invented figures: "a test AUC far above anything honest, and a first question on 'days since last spend' that separates churners almost perfectly" - or compute the leaky tree and add it to facts.json.

quote: It depends comes free, because every branch chooses its own next question.
problem: Read aloud without quotation marks this is not a sentence; I heard 'It depends' as the start of a clause and lost the rest.
fix: 'The tree handles it-depends patterns with no extra work, because every branch chooses its own next question.'

quote: Spend trend above 0.69, and then above 0.9 as well.
problem: Two full paths, six cut-offs and two counts by voice, with no reveal markers in the segment. Fine if the widget lights up each box as it is named; otherwise I am lost by the second path.
fix: Highlight each box in sync with the voice and round the counts ('about 200', 'about 3,400').

quote: So low activity matters far more when spend is also falling.
problem: With the table's numbers, quiet against active is 18 against 5 when spend holds (over three times) and 54 against 21 when it shrinks (under three times). It is 'far more' in points and less in ratio; a stakeholder would challenge me on it.
fix: Say which reading: 'in points, 13 more when spend holds, 33 more when it is falling'.

quote: Adding the creative ID as a column would fix it
problem: ID columns as a trap have not been taught yet; here they appear as a distractor, a line in the brief and a checklist item with nothing in the narration.
